newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mostly dip, CFDs ease 5 ct, fuel fl.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mostly dip, CFDs ease 5 ct, fuel fl.

text.p: European oil swaps were mostly weaker on Tuesday, tracking soft Brent futures which sunk 25 cents a barrel.

Brent CFDs lost ground again with next weeks dates trading from 62 cents down to 64 cents under June paper. This was about five cents down from late Monday, while the following two weeks lost a couple of cents.
Wet Brent also lost ground and the key May to June inter-month spread weakened ahead of the expiry of May IPE futures at the close of business on Tuesday.
Gasoline, which firmed on Monday and was well bid at the open, was little changed with May swaps around $195.50 a tonne.
Brokers said they expected renewed buying against Brent spreads over the next few days. "There is good demand for the cracks at these sort of levels," said one.
The third quarter crack spread was pegged around $4.10 a barrel but June was nearer $4.90.
Heavy fuel was little changed. Barges traded around $82.50 as a firmer Singapore offset the weakness on Rotterdam physical barges.
June was talked around $83.50 with July $84.50.
Gas oil crack spreads against Brent were flat at $4.35 for the third quarter with the three subsequent quarters at $4.90, $4.65 and $4.05 respectively.
Jet premiums firmed $1 a tonne to around $24 a tonne above the IPE for April and $25 above for May. The third quarter was $27.50 above and the fourth $33 above.
